Scenario fixture: landmark-unique

Each target has a stable id of the form lu_case_NN.

A. Valid

01 — NEUTRAL: two navs with distinct accessible names
Primary nav
Footer nav

B. Invalid

02 — CANTTELL: two navs share the same aria-label
First
Second
03 — NEUTRAL: unnamed <form role="search"> nested inside an unnamed role="search" container is not a second landmark; the <form> only counts as a landmark once it has an accessible name, same as its implicit-role counterpart
04 — CANTTELL: two named <form role="search"> elements sharing the same name ARE flagged (the name-gate only suppresses the unnamed case, it does not exempt <form> entirely)
05 — CANTTELL: two unnamed <aside> elements that are direct children of <main> ARE flagged — <main> is NOT "sectioning content" (only article/aside/nav/section are) and must not suppress <aside>'s implicit complementary role, unlike header/footer's "sectioning content plus main" rule
First sidebar
Second sidebar
06 — NEUTRAL: a NAMED <aside> nested inside real sectioning content (an <article>) is never suppressed — suppression only applies when an aside is BOTH nested in sectioning content AND unnamed
Related content
07 — NEUTRAL: two same-named navs where one copy is display:none (a responsive desktop/mobile duplicate pattern) — only landmarks actually exposed to assistive technology can collide
Visible copy
Hidden mobile copy
08 — CANTTELL: two aria-labelledby'd sections resolve to the same name via a NESTED descendant's aria-label, not the labelledby target's own textContent
Content
Content
09 — NEUTRAL: two navs distinguished only by a title attribute — title is a real accessible-name fallback source (aria-label > aria-labelledby > title)
Titled nav
Unnamed nav
10 — CANTTELL: two navs sharing the same title ARE flagged — title is a real naming source subject to the same duplicate-name check as aria-label/aria-labelledby, not exempt from it
First
Second
11 — NEUTRAL: two navs named via aria-labelledby pointing at a CSS-hidden (display:none) target with genuinely distinct text — per the accname spec, a directly-referenced labelledby target's hidden state does not block name computation, and the bypass covers its whole subtree, not just the target element itself
Product
First

12 — CANTTELL: two navs named via aria-labelledby pointing at a CSS-hidden target that resolve to the SAME text ARE still flagged — the hidden-target bypass (case 11) makes the name resolve at all, it does not exempt the result from the ordinary duplicate-name check
